subject: OneTrust Q&A pruning, archive plan & proof-chain mapping
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Emily Thompson <emily.thompson@acme.com>, vendr-support@vendr.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: OneTrust Q&A pruning, archive plan & proof-chain mapping

Emily / Vendr team —

Thanks again for the sync earlier. Per our discussion, Acme's OneTrust profile has ~420 Q&A answers that are duplicates or reference legacy attachments. Before we submit the CAIQ-derived fields to the portal, we want to: 

- prune stale Q&A entries (flagged answers >24 months)
- archive the original attachments into a signed-proof bucket and replace public attachments with a short placeholder (retention index)
- map each CAIQ question to a single canonical piece of evidence (proof-chain) so reviewers see an authoritative source rather than multiple partial files

I attached a quick export of the OneTrust Q&A and a first-pass retention matrix (onetrust_qna_export.zip, evidence_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx). Can Vendr confirm that replacing attachments with a stub (filename + retention index) keeps portal search and links intact? Also: will Whistic/OneTrust imports preserve the Q&A UID so we can maintain canonical mapping when we push the CAIQ fields?

Proposed timeline:
- Wed 6/16: final prune list delivered by Redwood
- Fri 6/19: Vendr to confirm import behavior and suggest a field mapping pattern
- Wed 6/24: mutual handoff — Redwood pushes CAIQ mapping CSV, Vendr validates import results in staging

Next steps for us: Ben is going to draft the CAIQ->proofchain CSV and Kimberly will coordinate the evidence removal windows with our internal PMs.

Thanks — please ping if any of those dates are tight.

Best,
Ava Chen
Security Programs | Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment(s): onetrust_qna_export.zip, evidence_retention_matrix_v1.xlsx

From: Emily Thompson <emily.thompson@acme.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: vendr-support@vendr.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OneTrust Q&A pruning, archive plan & proof-chain mapping

Thanks Ava — this plan makes sense. A couple quick points from Acme side:

1) The OneTrust UIDs are exported in the Q&A dump, so if you keep that column in your CAIQ mapping CSV we should be fine.
2) Archive approach: we need to retain the original hashes for audit; a stub that references a signed S3 object with a timestamp and SHA256 is acceptable.
3) Timeline: 6/16 is doable on our side but we'd prefer the handoff to be early in the day (EST) to give our security reviewers time to triage.

I can confirm with Vendr on whether the portal import will keep UID/stub links intact — tagging them here.

—Emily
Emily Thompson
Senior Governance Lead, Acme Analytics
emily.thompson@acme.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>, Emily Thompson <emily.thompson@acme.com>
Cc: vendr-support@vendr.com, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Jun 2026 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OneTrust Q&A pruning, archive plan & proof-chain mapping

Looping in my draft mapping. I attached caiaq_proofchain_draft.csv — column layout is: CAIQ_question_id | OneTrust_UID | canonical_evidence_filename | evidence_hash | retention_bucket_path | reviewer_note. The idea is to ensure each CAIQ field surfaces exactly one canonical file in the portal; duplicates point to the canonical file by UID.

Notes / questions:
- For items where the canonical evidence is a long runbook ( >10MB ), we propose linking to the signed S3 object rather than uploading the full PDF into OneTrust — saves on attachments and keeps the portal responsive.
- Vendr: can you surface the retention_bucket_path as a clickable profile field so reviewers can fetch the audit proof (S3 signed URL) without exposing the file on the portal?

Kimberly: I've added a proposed window for bulk removal (6/21 - 6/22) so platform owners have a 48h quiet period for changes. If that works I can start labeling the prune list with an "early-archive" tag for anything that meets the retention rules now.

Ben
Ben Carter
Portal Integrations | Redwood Inference

Attachment: caiaq_proofchain_draft.csv

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 13 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: OneTrust Q&A pruning, archive plan & proof-chain mapping

This looks good — thanks Ben. A couple small coordination items: 

- Please add an explicit column for ‘audit_owner’ in the CSV so we know who signs off post-migration.
- Acme: can you confirm the reviewer timezone preference for the 6/24 handoff? Ava, can we make that 10:00am EST / 7:00am PST so we have a full business day ahead of the weekly compliance review?
- Vendr-support: please confirm that a stub+signed-url pattern will keep search/indexing working. If there are portal-side field name constraints, flag them now so Ben can map accordingly.

Forwarding Emily’s note to reiterate the need for hashes and UIDs: 

> The OneTrust UIDs are exported in the Q&A dump, so if you keep that column in your CAIQ mapping CSV we should be fine.
> Archive approach: we need to retain the original hashes for audit; a stub that references a signed S3 object with a timestamp and SHA256 is acceptable.

I’ll update the shared Drive doc with the latest matrix and will add the audit_owner column. Link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3c-onetrust-prune-plan

—Kimberly
